texts.preamble: Ram Babu vs State Of U.P. And Another on 20 November, 2023 Author: Samit Gopal Bench: Samit Gopal High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:219806 Court No. - 69 Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 181 of 2012 Revisionist :- Ram Babu Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Revisionist :- Santosh Yadav Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt Advocate,C.K. Parekh Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J. Order on Criminal Misc. Recall Application No. 3 of 2023 1. List revised.
texts.arguments: 2. At the outset, learned counsel for the revisionist does not challenge his conviction, but submits that he is ready and willing to apply for commutation of sentence on the condition of further deposit, if any, in lieu of awarded sentence. Learned counsel further argued that the revisionist had disclosed his age as 60 years in the year 2009 before the trial court which was not disputed by the trial court, as of now he is aged about 74 years and is quite old and weak. 3. Learned counsel for the State submits that the sentence is proportionate to the charge established. He also submits that no useful purpose would be served by keeping this revision pending and it be disposed of by giving appropriate directions. 4. It is not disputed that the alleged offence took place on 03.06.1982, when the alleged sample of milk purchased from the revisionist was found to be adulterated. Learned A.G.A. is right in his submission that this Court cannot tinker, where minimum sentence is provided under a statute like the P.F.A. Act, 1954. 5. The Apex Court in the case of State of Rajasthan Vs. Jagdish Prasad : (2009) 12 SCC 646 held in paras-4 and 5 thereof as under: "4. In Dayal Singh v. State of Rajasthan it was inter alia observed as follows: (SCC pp. 728-29, para 15) "15. In the instant case it was not disputed that for the offence charged a minimum sentence of 6 months' rigorous imprisonment is prescribed by law. The appellant has been sentenced to undergo 6 months' rigorous imprisonment which is the minimum sentence. We are not inclined to modify the sentence by passing an order of the nature passed in N. Sukumaran Nair where this Court in exercise of its extraordinary jurisdiction imposed only a sentence of fine and directed that State to exercise its powers under Section 433 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to commute the sentence of simple imprisonment for fine.
